decision.thesis: All cash, the nineteenth all-cash row and first decision of ramp week 4, recorded after Tuesday 2026-09-29's closes on both markets and applied at Wednesday's first cached bars; the evening sweeps' rows for fundable names were read before it. NVIDIA (one lot 22.7% of equity): Monday's USD 150bn buyback increase (newsroom title 11:07Z; finnhub:142466054 08:25Z) is measured on the 2026-09-28 feedback page as idiosyncratic +3.02% at 1.65 sigma, the whole move in the opening gap (+2.08%) while AMD, INTC and AVGO fell; Tuesday closed 227.21 (-0.72% against SPY -0.18%), not yet decomposed; after Monday's close came an AI agent safety platform (techcrunch 21:00Z), an FT report of talks with insurers on AI financing risk (finnhub:142485020), a report that it and AMD lobbied against China export limits (finnhub:142496689), a Rosenblatt rating reaffirmation (marketbeat.com 12:22Z, title) and Reuters on why it sees its stock as good value (20:56Z), none with a figure the fact book holds. Maybank (24.5%): a new RM2.5bn AT1 sukuk reported after Monday's close (thestar 23:31Z, title only), then a Tuesday fall of 1.67% to 9.99. IHH (19.3%): 'Fortis buy was transparent' (thestar 23:05Z) and cooperation with the court-ordered audit (tipranks 09:52Z), titles only. Petronas Chemicals, Press Metal and Genting collected nothing. Bursa fell on Tuesday (^KLSE 1,670.02 to 1,643.96, -1.56%) with every fundable Bursa name lower, and that session is not decomposed; claim: nothing in the fundable universe beats cash over 21 sessions.
